title: Exercises
html:
Record your answers and bring them to the session.

Exercise 1: Assess someone else’s reasoning (15 mins)

Using the six points from the reasoning transparency lesson, assess Ord’s essay.

  • Does it state its conclusions up front?

  • Can you follow how he reached them?

  • Does it say how confident he is, and where he is uncertain?

  • Does it name its assumptions, or say what would change his mind?

  • How easily could you check the claims yourself?

Rate its reasoning transparency from 1 to 5 and note:

  • One thing it does well

  • One thing that could be clearer

  • One claim you would want more evidence for before being convinced

Exercise 2: Unpack your own reasoning (20 mins)

Think of a cause or charity you support, or would support if you had money to give. Anything counts: a food bank, a climate organisation, an animal welfare charity, medical research.

You will share this in the session. There is no right answer. The aim is to make your reasoning visible so that others can help you improve it.

Step 1: State your conclusion (2 mins)

Write one or two sentences: “I think [cause/charity] is a good place to direct resources because [core reason].”

Step 2: Trace your reasoning (8 mins)

  • How did you first learn about this cause or charity?

  • What experiences, conversations or information shaped your view?

  • What do you know about how effective it is? “Not much” is a valid answer.

  • How confident are you that this is a good use of resources? Give a rough percentage, or say “fairly confident” or “quite uncertain”.

Step 3: Identify your assumptions (5 mins)

What would need to be true for your reasoning to hold? For example:

  • “I’m assuming the charity uses donations efficiently”

  • “I’m assuming this problem is important relative to others”

  • “I’m assuming my friend who recommended it did their research”

What information, if you learned it, would change your mind?

Step 4: Reflect (5 mins)

Read back what you wrote. Was it harder than you expected? Did you find gaps you hadn’t noticed? Note anything you would like to discuss with the group.
